items.title: Current ownership and evidence matrix
items.text:
Python and Rust below mean the independent control libraries, not an audio backend that happens to use Python orchestration. Consumer tests supplement, rather than replace, shared standalone conformance.

Capability Python owner Rust owner Evidence / host boundary Definitions, units and references uFor canonical EnveLFO models Host-normalized native definitions uFor schema/codec/unit tests; Rust validates normalized definitions LFO playback, rate, reset, phase and onset enveLFO runtime Core LFO state Shared body traces and LFO tests; enge retains event-free sampling acceleration Finite/indefinite Envelopes, curved release and repeats enveLFO runtime Core Envelope state Shared runtime/host traces and focused Envelope tests Stage transitions, cue events and entry capture enveLFO runtime Core Stages state Shared body traces, command-preemption and partition tests Patch outputs, signal operators and retained state Standalone Patch scheduler Core Patch/signal modules Shared Patch/host traces and operator tests Division, offset, chance, random words and delayed queues Standalone Patch/random modules Core Patch/random modules Shared portable vectors and host traces; focused gate/cascade/capacity rollback tests Per-child clocks and elapsed beats versus song position Host TempoMap supplied to Patch Host ClockMapping supplied to Patch Shared stop/seek/tempo trace; frame conversion and clock acquisition stay in hosts Continuation and pending deliveries JSON snapshots Clones; optional core JSON snapshots Shared traces restore JSON with the Rust feature enabled; enge snapshot isolation and exact fractional delivery tests Voice scope, triggers, minimum hold and retirement enge enge Host policy, not duplicate Envelope playback Audio integration enge sampling and shared Python Patch state Native adapters over shared core state Full enge suite and Python/native Patch regressions arpeg expression integration Optional arpeg bridge Separate arpeg-envelfo crate Shared composition MIDI trace, mapped clocks and pending-delivery continuation

The legacy low-level ufor.lfo.LFO and its separate event/state/value records and initializer/query/command functions have been removed, with no aliases. enge block sampling consumes canonical LFO definitions and EnvelfoState directly. Lighting also uses that definition; stateless shape and activation mathematics remain in uFor without a runtime dependency cycle.

enge's named Envelope, LFO, Stages and retained Patch scheduling all consume the extracted library in both languages. NumPy spans, audio interpolation and native waveform kernels remain acceleration. enge still restricts amplitude profiles and curved native preparation; those are explicit host restrictions, not missing standalone Envelope capabilities.

items.title: Exact current reference boundary
items.text:
These public functions form the current scalar boundary:

  • initial_envelfo(use, at, seed=0) initializes LFO, Envelope, Stages, or SampleHold. References must already be materialized. Patch initialization uses the separate standalone envelfo.patch orchestration API.
  • envelfo_at(use, state, at) observes a scalar result. For Stages it computes an advance internally but returns only the value: a caller that needs events and continuation must retain the result of advance_envelfo instead.
  • envelfo_event(use, state, event) applies an ordered command and returns state. For Stages this delegates to advancement but does not return emitted events.
  • advance_envelfo(use, state, at, event=None) currently accepts only Stages and returns state, value and ordered events. It is not a general graph evaluator.
  • next_stage_event is a nonmutating natural-boundary query. Consumers must still perform advancement to obtain state transitions and emitted events.

Supported command sets are body-specific. For example, LFO rejects cue/sample, Envelope rejects cue/reset/transport/rate/sample, and transport-position LFO rejects phase commands. Do not silently add support or manufacture empty event lists for features that have no standalone event-emission API today.

items.title: Time and ordering
items.text:
Python boundary times and positions use Fraction, with explicit seconds or beats on the owning use. The same rational number in different clocks is not interchangeable. Integer audio frames and host conversion remain adapter inputs, not an implicit replacement for these clocks.

Elapsed-state queries cannot go back before their saved anchor. Commands must increase in (at, ordinal) order; separate ordinals allow multiple commands at one time. Direct transport-position LFO queries are different: at is song position, so a backward song seek can be observed without replaying history.

For staged advancement with a command, natural events strictly before its time are processed first, then the command. A command that changes stage at a natural boundary can discard the obsolete old-stage completion. Without such a change, eligible same-time natural boundaries are processed afterwards.

Natural markers at a named loop boundary precede cycle/turned. Named forward loop wraps emit both start and end markers at the wrap time in their existing marker order, including the final crossing. Ping-pong turns do not invent the opposite endpoint marker. These rules are already covered by uFor's test_named_envelope_loop_boundaries_preserve_markers_and_events.

Finite repeat counts count boundary crossings, including reversed crossings. The final crossing emits its boundary events then stage.done; an explicit finish transition additionally emits done. Without a finish transition, completion still holds the boundary value but does not invent a done event.

At inventory time the Rust runtime had f64 beat points, playback positions and delayed event times, and snapped near-integer staged event times using a tolerance. The native migration has removed that integration gap. The standalone boundary uses reduced signed i64 numerators and positive i64 denominators, with i128 intermediates and explicit errors when normalized components do not fit. It supports checked conversion to/from arpeg's Ratio<i64>; it does not promise arbitrary Python Fraction range. Command overflow leaves the supplied LFO state unchanged. Floating-point conversion is limited to signal values, not comparisons, phase wraps or position advancement. Rust supports cloned state and optional, self-contained versioned JSON through core's snapshots feature. This is not a shared Python/Rust wire format or a change to enge's audio snapshots.

items.title: Signals and observation schedules
items.text:
Results contain a floating value, activation weight, and exact status tag (idle, running, held, complete). The current scalar LFO returns its unweighted centered waveform and reports delay/fade through weight. A staged LFO applies fade to depth inside its value, preserves the center, and reports weight=1. These are distinct existing observable contracts. Do not normalize them during extraction or apply the fade twice in adapters.

Signal graphs are acyclic and evaluated in dependency order. Sum/Product/Affine do not implicitly clip to a modulation domain. Quantize half-step ties select the higher grid point. Patch signals remain dimensionless.

Latch, Threshold and Slew have observable state on a supplied observation grid. Threshold initializes silently and holds through its deadband. enge schedules resulting routed commands on the following frame; Slew receives the elapsed time per observation. Partition independence means identical logical observations and ordered inputs split across different calls. It does not mean changing that observation schedule leaves these operators unchanged.

The standalone graph evaluator consumes explicit host observations and next-delivery times through its Patch API, without an implicit audio grid or continuous-crossing detector. Ordinary LFO control interpolation is also a host optimization, not the definition of exact LFO/Staged LFO observations.

items.title: Events, randomness and state
items.text:
Keep connection declaration order, every/offset counters, random streams and pending deliveries as state. Division happens before chance testing; probability zero/one does not consume a random draw. Number source occurrences from zero: an occurrence is eligible when index >= offset and (index - offset) % every == 0. Thus every=3, offset=0 selects musician-facing occurrences 1, 4, 7; offset=2 selects 3, 6, 9, and offsets larger than the division are an initial skip, not reduced modulo that division. Chance compares the upper 53 random bits against int(probability * 2**53) after division.

SplitMix64 advances modulo 2**64. Signal draws use the upper 53 bits. The existing stream-key byte prefix is ufor-envelfo-v1 followed by a zero byte; renaming the package must not change it or the seed/identity encoding. uFor traces already call stream_key to assign voice keys, so that portable identity helper must remain usable by uFor without importing the runtime. Random draw execution can move to enveLFO; do not move all seed derivation behind an envelfo -> ufor -> envelfo dependency cycle.

Preserve current staged event and host connection/queue capacity errors (4096 limits at their existing enforcement points). These are not a new global graph-size guarantee. Unsupported scope, curves, or Patch-level commands remain explicit errors until a separately tested implementation supports them.

JSON restoration of Python scalar state and restoration of native aggregate state are distinct existing contracts. Preserve equivalent continuation in each. Cross-language snapshot interchange is not required by this baseline.

items.title: Extraction ownership map
items.text:
uFor enveLFO enge/adapters Definitions, score registration, unit validation, reference materialization, structural port/range checks, portable event/state records Initialization, body/state advancement, command execution, boundary scheduling, retained graph state, random draws, event connection execution Voice/context allocation, trigger-to-instance addressing, minimum-hold release policy, audio modulation mapping, output buffers and renderer snapshots Format mathematics needed by validation, including quantizer range calculations and declared shape/time helpers Pure graph orchestration shared by ControlRenderer and standalone hosts NumPy block acceleration and native/PyO3 conversion Portable stream identity construction used by traces Independent Rust control types and equivalent execution, with a fixture reader for conformance Aggregation of audio and control states at the consumer boundary

Each algorithm must have one implementation per language after extraction. Do not leave uFor evaluation copies or a second enge native implementation. Definition helpers needed for validation stay dependency-safe and are reused, not duplicated under new names. Portable state records remaining in uFor do not authorize uFor to depend on their executing library.

items.title: Shared fixtures and verification
items.text:
The sibling enveLFO repository owns envelfo-runtime.json, envelfo-patch.json, envelfo-host.json and envelfo-streams.json. Both standalone implementations read them directly. Exact times, events, pending delivery boundaries and random words compare exactly; signal values use absolute tolerance 1e-12 and zero relative tolerance. Expectations are handwritten from simple waveform/time/order rules, not generated by one backend.

The host corpus covers mixed clocks, running versus stopped beats, forward and backward song seeks, direct song-position signals, delayed capture while transport is stopped, seconds-based Slew, division/offset sampling, curved Envelope commands, and pending deliveries across continuation. The Rust fixture host integrates supplied observations only; it is not a new core tempo API.

Python restore steps serialize and reload state. With snapshots enabled, the Rust shared body/Patch/host traces serialize and reload every continuation step; default Rust builds retain clone-based continuation checks. Cross-language snapshot interchange is not required. arpeg owns its composed expression wire trace and verifies its explicit lane ownership and same-time delivery phases independently of enge.

The audit verifies clean wheel installation outside the source tree without NumPy/enge, source-distribution and standalone crate builds, Python 3.13/3.15 on macOS, Rust debug/release tests and consumer suites. Cross-platform checks remain release-only; configuring them is not evidence that a release has passed. No release or hardware validation is implied.

items.title: Separately scoped follow-ups
items.text:
Optional Rust JSON snapshots now cover LFO, Envelope, Stages, SampleHold and Patch definitions plus complete state, including pending core deliveries and RNG streams. Hosts still save clock mappings and external queues themselves. This does not add serialized combined enge/arpeg application snapshots.

arpeg's Python and Rust players now separate scheduling and MIDI realization. Hosts deliver same-time hits, observe the bridge once, then realize controllers before note-on, retaining existing release and expression-lane ownership rules. Python snapshots also retain pending unrealized batches. Combined Rust host snapshot serialization remains separate work.

Standalone Python bindings to Rust remain optional. Built-in Rust tempo acquisition and broader audio-host Envelope profiles are not silently added here.

items.title: Scope
items.text: This audit covers the block path introduced by PersistentSynth, PersistentFM, PersistentNoise, PersistentSampler, LiveEngine, native effects, and the bounded action queue. It distinguishes measured callback-shaped performance from the stronger allocation-free, lock-free, and Python-free contract in the completed live-effects implementation.

items.title: Current boundary
items.text: The oscillator, FM, and noise runtimes retain voices, controls, LFOs, filters, routing, and snapshots in Rust. Their process_actions_into entry point writes to caller-owned output. This does not establish an allocation-free contract for every supported profile; the Patch migration and remaining qualification are detailed below. The fixed-size action queue uses rtrb, publishes whole batches, and drains only the batch prefix visible when draining starts. Control ramps and instrument/part/trigger context storage are owned by the shared native ControlBank; its storage is prepared before processing and retained in generated-source snapshots.

items.title: Patch scheduler allocation boundary
items.text:
The 2026-11-03 audit found temporary input/release vectors, copied names and allocating shared Patch calls. The approved migration now pins envelfo-core revision 2f2ffb0a5fe45f37b7a67d602e7b7eafa908e259 and uses its prepared transaction storage for observation, commands, settling and voice reset. Live-source construction prepares all slots before processing. Retirement retains their state and capacity; snapshot restoration rebuilds processing storage outside rendering. Input updates and ordered release scans no longer allocate lists. Each slot permits 4096 pending connections; no named event outputs leave this host, so its external event buffer has zero capacity.

Shared-core allocation tests cover reset, observation, cues, delayed events, capacity rollback, cloning and snapshot continuation. Enge's full native callback still needs allocation qualification across onset, observation, addressed commands, scheduled child events and release. Native sampler generators remain rejected until their integration is implemented; these shared-core results alone do not qualify that profile or establish hardware deadlines.

LiveRuntime owns processing for generated and sampled sources. It owns cloned oscillator, FM, and noise runtimes, immutable sample assets and traversal cursors, one bounded action queue per source, and preallocated source/mix/output scratch. Its processing body releases the GIL, captures each queue's published prefix at entry, advances a prepared gain/multiply/filter/granulator graph with exact sample-offset parameter ramps, and latches failures before copying output to NumPy. The graph's parameters, recursive filters, circular grain history, active grain pool, and ramps participate in snapshots. The Python method is a callback conformance harness; a native host can call the same Rust processing body directly.

The complete LiveEngine path is not yet ready for a system audio callback:

  • Python validates and encodes uFor actions, sorts each block, refreshes active slot/context lists, and mixes source arrays.
  • LiveEngine.advance_into() currently calls the allocating advance() path.
  • The higher-level PersistentSampler still orchestrates its general dynamic control/filter profile in Python. NativeLiveEngine directly encodes the tuning/gain/envelope/traversal profile and multichannel filter chains. Filter banks are prepared per voice, reset on reuse and retained in snapshots. Unsupported dynamic sample settings are rejected during setup. The sampler adapter prepares scoped amplitude/tuning, cutoff/Q and crossfade controls through set_sample_controls and admits addressed actions before native processing. Context and route scratch storage remain bounded; snapshot ownership includes the Python addresses and native control state.
  • OfflineEffects still builds parameter and output arrays for every block. The live adapter now prepares the supported graph once and encodes parameter and bypass actions into bounded batches, but LiveEngine does not yet own and submit those batches.
  • The Python ActionQueue binding is a deterministic single-thread harness. A native host must own the rtrb producer and consumer on separate threads.

NativeLiveEngine is the control-side harness for all four source families. It validates and encodes oscillator, FM, noise, and supported sampler trace actions plus effect actions, submits bounded batches, then invokes the single Rust owner. This removes Python DSP, mixing, and effect-array construction from its callback body. Python still performs admission and submission synchronously before that call. Native sampler key/velocity event bindings use preallocated per-voice values, initialized during onset admission and retained in snapshots. The native sampler profile currently excludes generators. Generated synth, FM and noise velocity bindings use the same native per-voice storage. Their Python onset metadata shares bounded trigger-context ownership and is included in source snapshots. Control-routed sampler filters reuse the fixed bank's stage kernel and retain preallocated per-voice integrators; parameter evaluation does not allocate.

Granulators allocate circular history and a fixed captured-grain pool during setup. Duration, density, lookback, playback ratio, jitter, wet/dry, bypass, and snapshot continuation stay inside the owner without growing callback storage. Freeze and unfreeze actions preserve their state across snapshots and match the reference's circular replay. Frozen source positions wrap through a 64-frame tail/head overlap, reduced only when a startup freeze has fewer valid frames, and active grains retain captured samples across unfreeze.

These are correctness and integration milestones, not hidden real-time claims. The next implementation boundaries are expanding the native sampler profile if live sample modulation requires it and a native host that owns producer and callback threads without Python entry. Those paths must use the existing borrowed input/output and preallocated scratch model rather than wrapping their allocating Python entry points.

items.title: Stress harness
items.text:
scripts/benchmark_live.py renders a prepared 16-voice triangle synth through a gain and resonant-filter chain using NativeLiveEngine and a caller-owned stereo buffer. It submits 64 admitted effect actions at every block boundary, including interrupted gain and cutoff ramps. --granular adds bounded granulation, density changes, and one freeze/unfreeze transition per second. The harness includes control-side block admission, queue submission, and the single native processing call; it excludes device I/O and initial event preparation. It discards the first callback and reports median, p99, maximum, and maximum fraction of the hard block budget. A good timing result does not waive the host and device blockers above.

Run it with:

uv run python scripts/benchmark_live.py --block-frames 64 --seconds 10 --voices 16
uv run python scripts/benchmark_live.py --block-frames 64 --seconds 10 --voices 16 --granular

On 2026-09-23, the local arm64 macOS development build completed 7,500 callbacks with a 64-frame block, 16 voices, and 64 effect actions per callback. Excluding the first callback, the gain-plus-filter profile had a 275.1-microsecond median, 482.0-microsecond p99, and 2,017.2-microsecond maximum against a 1,333.3-microsecond block budget. The one observed maximum exceeded the deadline.

With the same action density and bounded granulator enabled, the second run had a 266.6-microsecond median, 403.8-microsecond p99, and 1,157.1-microsecond maximum, or 86.8 percent of the block budget. These development-host measurements establish the cost of the current Python admission harness. The outlier reinforces that it is not a native host deadline guarantee.

persistent-16-voice owns all oscillator phases, routing, filter integrators, and gain state in one Rust object and crosses Python once per block. filter, filter-actions, subnormal, and fanout execute one whole graph per Rust call. The action case submits the maximum 64 actions at every block boundary. The subnormal case scales source output by 1e-310. filter-tail ends every graph halfway through the run and measures the reference tail path. granulator and freeze execute the Rust granular kernel, including bounded frozen-history circular replay. filter+granulator currently uses the NumPy graph because the offline native graph kernel does not compose granulation with other processors. That row still measures Python orchestration rather than a callback-safe native graph.

This harness includes Python source/action orchestration around native DSP and therefore measures the current callable system rather than a GIL-free native host. It does not test a lock-free action queue, bounded callback error status, tail-pool retirement, a physical audio device, or thread-local subnormal handling. Those items remain required before enge can claim live callback readiness.

items.title: MIDI performance binding conversion
items.text: enge.performance.MidiConverter is a caller-driven MIDI 1 adapter. It accepts decoded meedee messages and emits uFor Trigger, Release and ControlChange values. It opens no files, devices or audio streams and starts no threads. enge.midi.read_midi() supplies file timing to configured converters. Live transport and audio-clock integration remain host responsibilities.

items.title: Preparation and reference ownership
items.text:
Construct one converter per independent input source. Supply a PerformanceBindingScore and its resolved SynthInstrumentScore or SampleInstrumentScore. Synth, FM and noise share the synth instrument model. The host resolves score references, verifies any hashes and ensures that the supplied instrument is the referenced target. This adapter does not introduce another score loader or infer identity from document names. The host must serialize feed, loss, finish and restart calls on each instance; the converter does not add threads or locks.

For each referenced tuning, supply its resolved uFor Tuning body in tunings, keyed by ScoreReference.key: a relative path, or selector: followed by the selector. Missing referenced tunings fail preparation. With no tuning reference, notes use 12-tone equal temperament with A4 at 440 Hz. Finite tunings do not wrap or fall back to equal temperament when a key is unavailable.

Preparation snapshots the binding and used tunings, and checks every CC/bend target and output range against the instrument's control declarations. It does not synthesize initial controller observations. Defaults remain the engine's responsibility. Input channels are 1–16; output parts are the binding's named parts rather than channel numbers. Several channels can share a part, while their note-pairing queues remain separate.

items.title: Feeding messages
items.text:
from enge.performance import MidiConverter

converter = MidiConverter(
    source="keyboard-a",
    binding=binding,
    instrument=instrument,
    tunings=resolved_tunings,
)
events = converter.feed(message, tick=destination_tick, ordinal=input_ordinal)

The host supplies integer destination ticks and nonnegative integer ordinals. Pairs (tick, ordinal) must increase strictly, including ignored messages; ordinals need only disambiguate equal ticks. Ticks can be negative for preroll. No timestamps are rounded, clocks guessed or units converted. The host owns any native-clock mapping and conversion to instrument frames.

Every nonzero NoteOn produces a fresh trigger identity with the source prefix. Source names follow uFor identifier rules and must distinguish converter instances whose outputs could be combined, including recreated instances. restart() keeps the instance's ID counter, so abandoned identities are not reused. NoteOff and zero-velocity NoteOn release the oldest or newest held identity as selected by the binding, independently for each channel/key. Velocity populates Trigger.velocity; no named velocity control is invented.

CC values follow the binding's declared linear ranges. Optional pitch bend uses the explicit minimum/center/maximum mapping in uFor's contract, reaching the endpoints exactly. It emits a named part control and does not modify trigger pitch itself. Unselected channels, unmapped CCs and unconfigured bend have no effect. Program changes, pressure, timing messages and SysEx have no conversion in this source profile. They return an empty list; the host may process them separately. Sustain is only a mapped control, not an implicit converter note-lifetime rule. UMP messages and compound commands are rejected explicitly; a shared Message base does not make them primitive MIDI 1 input.

items.title: Failure and restart
items.text:
The default max_held_notes=4096 bounds held identities across all selected channels. A host may choose a different positive integer. Released identities leave the budget even if an engine is still sounding a sustained voice or tail. This is not an engine voice limit or a total-memory/CPU guarantee; definitions, identifier lengths, integer sizes and application-retained outputs also cost resources. There is no growing registry of sources or previously emitted events.

Overflow, unmatched releases, unavailable tuning notes, out-of-order input, MIDI System Reset and unsupported message families raise ValueError, discard pairing state and require an explicit restart(). Later conversion attempts raise RuntimeError until then. Ordinary argument validation rejects invalid values before consuming the input. When a transport/decoder reports loss, the host must call report_loss(); missing MIDI traffic is not independently detectable here.

finish() verifies that all observed notes were released and stops the instance until restart; unreleased notes are an error. Neither failure, loss, finish nor restart emits releases or restores controls. The host retains responsibility for downstream voices and musical recovery. Never treat restarting observation as evidence that an instrument is silent or synchronized.

items.title: MIDI-file import and rendering
items.text:
read_midi(path, *, converters=[...], sample_rate=48000) requires at least one ready converter. ready is true on construction or after an explicit restart; an instance already fed messages or finished is not ready. Read-only source and parts describe the converter's configured routing. Source names and part names must be distinct across converters. Channels may overlap across converters for deliberate layering; channels sharing a part within one converter remain supported. Each converter retains its own held-note budget.

The importer checks arguments and routing before opening the file. It supports synchronous PPQN SMF types 0/1, merges tracks stably, accumulates tempo with exact rational arithmetic and rounds absolute times to frames, ties to even. Metadata and track ends retain their timing effects, including trailing silence. SysEx and escape file records are rejected: an escape record could contain arbitrary MIDI traffic rather than a decoded SysEx message. Type 2 and SMPTE remain unsupported by this adapter. The existing meedee reader defaults apply: 1 MiB per record, 128 tracks and 8 MiB of merge lookahead.

Every primitive message is fed to each converter. Its binding chooses notes, tuning, pairing and CC/bend semantics. Unmapped controls and pressure are ignored, replacing the former importer's hard-coded rejection policy. Positive bend now reaches its declared maximum at +8191 rather than falling slightly short.

MidiPerformance.parts maps binding names to event lists, including configured parts with no events. No channel numbers are inferred as part names. The importer finishes every converter on success. A failed file read, conversion, finish or interruption invalidates all participating converters and returns no partial performance. Argument/routing rejection before reading leaves their state alone. There is no implicit restart, retry or rollback of previously emitted identities.

Prepare an instrument once with Patch.prepare_score(sample_rate) or supply an equivalent resolved (score, assets) pair. Use the score to configure its converter and pass that same pair to render_midi, keyed by the part name. The Bach example resolves selectors from its fixed in-memory instrument map; there is no implicit library discovery or score-file loading.

The renderer requires one instrument per configured part, matching sample rates and the stereo left, right layout. It selects oscillator/FM/noise from the resolved voice type or uses the sampler for sample scores. Existing engine preparation rejects unsupported mixed-engine scores. Output retains the 250 ms tail budget; a voice still active afterward fails rendering before publication. Presets consume Trigger.velocity through uFor's velocity event binding, not a synthetic named control. Offline oscillator, FM and noise rendering retain onset velocity in their shared control-context snapshots; sampler slot velocities continue to use the sampler's resolved onset values. Persistent oscillator/FM/ noise renderers retain their existing supported binding profile.

items.title: Caller-polled live input
items.text:
enge.midi.LiveInput(connection, converters=[...], message_limit=128) wraps a caller-owned, queue-mode MIDI 1.0 meedee.midi.TypedInputConnection. UMP is unsupported by this converter and fails explicitly. Configure fresh or explicitly restarted converters with distinct source names and destination parts, as for file import. Use one adapter per independent input connection. The host opens and closes the connection, selects meedee's isolation mode and must be its only queue consumer. Do not share its converters with another active adapter or file import. The adapter adds no queue, thread or audio-device ownership.

Call drain(frame=destination_frame) on one host control thread. It polls at most message_limit typed items without waiting for MIDI, including ignored messages, and returns a dictionary of named parts with their ordered uFor events. Frames must be integers and must not decrease; equal frames retain input order through increasing ordinals across calls. Every message in a drain receives that frame. Backend timestamps are not mapped to an audio clock. This is block-quantized scheduling, not a hard real-time audio callback API.

The adapter checks receive-drop counts, connection failure and closure before and after receiving. Any observed loss, decoder diagnostic, conversion failure or interruption invalidates all participating converters, permanently stops the adapter and discards that drain's result. In isolated mode drop updates are asynchronous: detection cannot retract events returned by an earlier drain. Silence alone does not establish device health. Previously returned events and musical cleanup remain the host's responsibility.

stop() is idempotent and invalidates conversion state. It sends no messages, closes no ports and generates no releases. Recovery requires a fresh healthy connection, fresh or explicitly restarted converters, and a new adapter. Do not reuse queued events from a failed session. The adapter does not produce sound or add an audio-device host.

For supervised macOS qualification using only temporary test-created virtual endpoints in both process modes, run explicitly:

uv run --frozen pytest -q -s -n 0 test/qualification/midi_input.py

Each native case has a 45-second outer deadline. The checks cover note/control/ bend conversion, release pairing, host-frame ordering, caller-owned close and receive loss followed by silence. They do not qualify physical devices or other operating systems.

items.title: Measuring
items.text:
Run only one benchmark or test suite at a time. Use the same interpreter, native build, worker count, and test selection for before/after comparisons. Keep other projects' test runs idle. Profiler timings include substantial instrumentation overhead and are not ordinary test timings.

uv run pytest --durations=30
uv run pytest -n 0 test/test_control.py
uv run python -m cProfile -o /private/tmp/enge-latch.prof -m pytest -n 0 -q \
  'test/test_envelfo_latch.py::test_latch_captures_delivery_frame_with_independent_gates_and_snapshot[1.0-lfo-numpy]'

Read the profile without launching the engine:

printf 'sort cumulative\nstats (control.py|lfo.py|synth.py) 20\nquit\n' | \
  uv run python -m pstats /private/tmp/enge-latch.prof

The full suite remains the commit gate. Selecting individual tests is for development feedback, not a replacement for complete conformance checks. Linux and Windows validation remains release-only.

items.title: Findings, 2026-10-11
items.text:
Measurements on macOS with Python 3.13.12, pytest 9.1.1, pytest-xdist 3.8.0, and the default native build without the optional Rubber Band feature:

  • Baseline full suite: 352.74 seconds, 1,082 passed and 21 optional skips, with ten workers and work-stealing.
  • Optimized full suite: 323.88 seconds, 1,085 passed and the same 21 optional skips, with the same ten-worker setup. This single before/after comparison saved 28.86 seconds, approximately 8%. The three additional cases cover single-frame cancellation and malformed/nonfinite signals.
  • Representative Latch test under cProfile: 27.95 seconds before optimization, 16.60 seconds afterward. This is approximately 41% less test time.
  • The profile identified repeated enveLFO-to-renderer-LFO model validation, one-frame LFO span generation, and one-element modulation arrays as bottlenecks. WAV regression writing was not a significant cost in this profile.

The worker experiment used the following unchanged 38-case selection. Run it sequentially with four, six, and ten workers:

uv run pytest -n 4 --durations=5 \
  test/test_envelfo_latch.py::test_latch_activation_and_same_frame_captures \
  test/test_envelfo_quantize.py \
  test/test_control.py::test_array_modulation_matches_scalar_routes_and_weights

Four workers took 22.60 seconds, six took 20.69, and ten took 21.02. These are single runs on one host, not a universal worker recommendation. The small six-versus-ten difference does not justify changing the portable -n auto default. Re-measure when hardware, Python, or the test workload changes. After optimization, the same 38-case selection with ten workers took 15.19 seconds, versus 21.02 beforehand, approximately 28% less time.

items.title: Changes and coverage
items.text:
The renderer retains converted immutable LFO definitions for its lifetime. Exact one-frame NumPy LFO queries reuse uFor's scalar evaluator; interpolated sine queries still use their event-anchored interpolation grid. Native LFO queries still execute the Rust kernel. One-frame modulation uses the existing uFor scalar evaluator, while multi-frame queries remain vectorized. Stateful Patch output is filled into preallocated arrays instead of retaining every one-frame result dictionary until concatenation.

Envelfo tests share read-only, session-local reference audio for the same plain square-wave instrument. Randomized Envelfo output, snapshots, partitioning, and NumPy/native/persistent comparisons are still evaluated separately. No persistent disk cache or new dependency is introduced.

The routing arithmetic test uses explicit clamping and knot-boundary inputs instead of 48,001 scalar queries. It also compares single-frame and block results. Linear, step, and exponential mappings, activation weights, validation, and cancellation retain coverage. Audio regressions continue to generate at least one second of 48 kHz WAV output; none have been shortened or removed.

items.title: Stages and event-processing follow-up
items.text:
The first pass did not remove the dominant cost. A representative staged-clock and cue-routing regression took 51.84 seconds under cProfile, with roughly 688,000 advance_envelfo calls. Its event-processing method accounted for 51.23 seconds of the test. Most calls merely advanced state through frames that contained no events.

uv run python -m cProfile -o /private/tmp/enge-stages.prof -m pytest -n 0 -q \
  'test/test_lfo_instrument.py::test_patch_division_is_first_aligned_independent_and_snapshot_safe[1-0.5-0-0-0-False-divisors0-cue-stages]'

The follow-up renders event-free seconds-clock intervals using the existing LFO and linear-envelope block kernels. uFor's natural-boundary query determines where the next stage event occurs. LFO markers and queued deliveries also bound each interval. The original delivery loop still processes those events at exact fractional times, including multiple events observed on one frame. State is advanced to the last observed frame of each interval, preserving snapshot and subsequent-command timing.

Staged LFO values remain exact even when the host requests interpolated ordinary LFO controls. Delay/fade weights are applied inside the staged value, as in the scalar reference. Beat clocks, nonlinear or reversing envelopes, and per-frame Latch/Threshold/Slew observation retain their existing evaluation path. The optimization does not remove these cases or change their coverage. Block eligibility is checked for all participating Envelfos before allocating arrays. A mixed block/scalar-only configuration therefore does not perform block-sized allocations repeatedly on every frame.

The dependency refresh is committed separately from renderer changes. It includes the public uFor boundary query and aligns enge's reccy package-source URL with uFor's HTTPS source; repository Git remotes remain SSH.

items.title: Final measurements
items.text:
• Dependency-only baseline, before event-span rendering: 282.11 seconds, 1,085 passed and 21 optional skips.
  • Final full suite: 114.70 seconds, 1,091 passed and the same 21 optional skips. This saves 167.41 seconds, about 59%, against the matched dependency baseline, or about 67% against the original 352.74-second run. Both comparisons use ten workers and work-stealing on the same macOS/Python 3.13 host.
  • An earlier optimized full run passed 1,089 cases in 121.27 seconds, before adding the two mixed-mode regressions and final block-eligibility check.
  • The final representative profiled Stages case took 0.95 seconds, versus 51.84 seconds before. advance_envelfo calls fell from 688,264 to 624; event-processing time fell from 51.23 seconds to 0.09 seconds.
  • All 1,206 uFor tests passed for the boundary-query change. The six new enge cases cover exact staged LFO delay/fade under control intervals and single-frame partitions, plus mixed staged LFO/looping-Envelope evaluation.

Full-suite timings are single-host measurements, not cross-platform guarantees. The remaining slowest cases involve per-frame threshold/slew observations and beat-clock evaluation. No regression duration, backend comparison, or existing test was removed to obtain the improvement.

items.title: control_samples(state: ControlState, start: int, frames: int, rate: int) -> np.ndarray
items.text:
Resolve exact anchors once, then generate the linear ramp in arrays.

Source code in enge/control.py 
def control_samples(
    state: ControlState, start: int, frames: int, rate: int
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Resolve exact anchors once, then generate the linear ramp in arrays."""
    output = np.full(frames, state.target, dtype=np.float64)
    if not frames:
        return output
    elapsed = Fraction(start, rate) - state.at
    if elapsed < 0:
        raise ValueError("Control query precedes current state")
    if state.value == state.target or elapsed >= state.smoothing:
        return output
    count = min(frames, ceil((state.smoothing - elapsed) * rate))
    progress = (float(elapsed * rate) + np.arange(count)) / float(
        state.smoothing * rate
    )
    output[:count] = state.value + (state.target - state.value) * progress
    return output

items.title: modulation_samples(definition: modulation.Modulation, signals: dict[str, np.ndarray], frames: int) -> dict[tuple[str, str], np.ndarray]
items.text:
Evaluate blocks in arrays and single observations with uFor's scalar math.

Source code in enge/control.py 
def modulation_samples(
    definition: modulation.Modulation, signals: dict[str, np.ndarray], frames: int
) -> dict[tuple[str, str], np.ndarray]:
    """Evaluate blocks in arrays and single observations with uFor's scalar math."""
    sources = {s.name: s for s in definition.sources}
    for name, signal in signals.items():
        if name not in sources:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown modulation source {name}")
        source = sources[name]
        if signal.shape != (frames, 2) or not np.all(np.isfinite(signal)):
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid modulation signal {name}")
        if np.any((signal[:, 0] < source.minimum) | (signal[:, 0] > source.maximum)):
            raise ValueError(f"source {name} value is outside its domain")
        if np.any((signal[:, 1] < 0) | (signal[:, 1] > 1)):
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid modulation weight {name}")
    if frames == 1:
        values = modulation.evaluate(
            definition,
            {
                n: modulation.SourceValue(value=float(s[0, 0]), weight=float(s[0, 1]))
                for n, s in signals.items()
            },
        )
        return {
            (v.target.name, v.target.parameter): np.array([v.value]) for v in values
        }
    additions: dict[modulation.Target, list[np.ndarray]] = {
        p.target: [] for p in definition.parameters
    }
    products = {p.target: np.ones(frames) for p in definition.parameters}
    for route in sorted(definition.routes, key=lambda r: (r.source, r.name)):
        if route.source not in signals:
            raise ValueError(f"missing modulation source {route.source}")
        signal = signals[route.source]
        knots = np.array([p.input for p in route.points])
        amounts = np.array([p.amount for p in route.points])
        index = np.clip(
            np.searchsorted(knots, signal[:, 0], side="right") - 1, 0, len(knots) - 1
        )
        mapped = amounts[index]
        if route.interpolation != modulation.Interpolation.step and len(knots) > 1:
            lower = np.minimum(index, len(knots) - 2)
            progress = np.clip(
                (signal[:, 0] - knots[lower]) / (knots[lower + 1] - knots[lower]), 0, 1
            )
            if route.interpolation == modulation.Interpolation.exponential:
                mapped = np.exp(
                    (1 - progress) * np.log(amounts[lower])
                    + progress * np.log(amounts[lower + 1])
                )
            else:
                mapped = amounts[lower] + progress * (
                    amounts[lower + 1] - amounts[lower]
                )
            mapped = np.where(signal[:, 0] <= knots[0], amounts[0], mapped)
            mapped = np.where(signal[:, 0] >= knots[-1], amounts[-1], mapped)
        if route.operation == modulation.Operation.add:
            additions[route.target].append(signal[:, 1] * mapped)
        else:
            products[route.target] *= 1 + signal[:, 1] * (mapped - 1)
    output = {}
    for parameter in definition.parameters:
        value = (
            parameter.default + _sum(additions[parameter.target], frames)
        ) * products[parameter.target]
        if np.any(
            ~np.isfinite(value)
            | (value < parameter.minimum)
            | (value > parameter.maximum)
        ):
            raise ValueError(
                f"modulated {parameter.target.name}.{parameter.target.parameter} "
                "is outside its domain"
            )
        output[parameter.target.name, parameter.target.parameter] = value
    return output

class ParameterRamp(BaseModel):
    at: int
    start: float
    target: float
    duration: int = Field(ge=0)

    def value(self, frame: int) -> float:
        if frame >= self.at + self.duration or self.duration == 0:
            return self.target
        return self.start + (self.target - self.start) * (
            (frame - self.at) / self.duration
        )

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", allow_inf_nan=False)

class OfflineEffects:
    """Process one graph with exact frame actions and explicit input endings."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        definition: PreparedEffects,
        backend: Literal["numpy", "native"] = "numpy",
    ) -> None:
        if backend not in ("numpy", "native"):
            raise EngineError(f"Unknown effect backend: {backend}")
        self.definition = definition.model_copy(deep=True)
        self.backend = backend
        self.frame = 0
        self.ended_inputs: dict[str, int] = {}
        self.stopped_at: int | None = None
        layouts = _processor_layouts(definition.definition)
        self.processors = {
            p.name: _initial_state(p, len(layouts[p.name]), self.definition.sample_rate)
            for p in definition.definition.processors
        }

    def advance(
        self,
        inputs: dict[str, np.ndarray],
        actions: list[audio_effects.EffectAction],
        start: int,
        end: int,
    ) -> np.ndarray:
        """Process `[start, end)`; every input covers that exact frame interval."""
        if start != self.frame or end < start:
            raise EngineError("Effect advance must be contiguous")
        frames = end - start
        graph = self.definition.definition
        if frames > graph.maximum_block_frames:
            raise EngineError("Effect block exceeds its prepared maximum")
        expected = {i.name: len(i.channels) for i in graph.inputs}
        if inputs.keys() != expected.keys():
            raise EngineError("Effect inputs do not match the prepared graph")
        source_audio: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}
        for name, channels in expected.items():
            value = np.asarray(inputs[name], dtype=np.float64)
            if value.shape != (frames, channels) or not np.all(np.isfinite(value)):
                raise EngineError(f"Invalid effect input {name}")
            source_audio[name] = value
        if frames == 0:
            if actions:
                raise EngineError("Zero-frame effect calls cannot contain actions")
            return np.zeros((0, len(self.definition.channels)))
        if any(a.tick < start or a.tick >= end for a in actions):
            raise EngineError("Effect action is outside the render interval")
        if any(
            (b.tick, b.ordinal) <= (a.tick, a.ordinal)
            for a, b in zip(actions, actions[1:], strict=False)
        ):
            raise EngineError("Effect actions must be strictly ordered")
        action_index = 0
        output = np.zeros((frames, len(self.definition.channels)))
        try:
            if (
                self.backend == "native"
                and not any(
                    isinstance(
                        a, (audio_effects.InputEndAction, audio_effects.StopAction)
                    )
                    for a in actions
                )
                and not self.ended_inputs
                and _native_supported(self.processors, graph, actions)
            ):
                output = self._advance_native(source_audio, actions, start, end)
                self.frame = end
                return output
            for i in range(frames):
                frame = start + i
                while (
                    action_index < len(actions) and actions[action_index].tick == frame
                ):
                    self._apply(actions[action_index])
                    action_index += 1
                if self.stopped_at is not None:
                    continue
                audio, ended = self._process_frame(source_audio, i, frame)
                if ended:
                    self.stopped_at = frame
                else:
                    output[i] = audio
        except (ValueError, FloatingPointError) as error:
            self.stopped_at = start
            output.fill(0)
            raise EngineError(
                f"Effect processing failed in block at frame {start}"
            ) from error
        if not np.all(np.isfinite(output)):
            self.stopped_at = start
            output.fill(0)
            raise EngineError(f"Non-finite effect output in block at frame {start}")
        self.frame = end
        return output

    def _advance_native(
        self,
        input_audio: dict[str, np.ndarray],
        actions: list[audio_effects.EffectAction],
        start: int,
        end: int,
    ) -> np.ndarray:
        from . import _native

        graph = self.definition.definition
        processors = {p.name: p for p in graph.processors}
        ordered = [processors[n] for n in self.definition.order]
        if len(ordered) == 1 and isinstance(
            processor := ordered[0], audio_effects.Granulator
        ):
            return self._advance_native_granulator(
                processor, input_audio, actions, start, end
            )
        input_indices = {v.name: i for i, v in enumerate(graph.inputs)}
        processor_indices = {
            p.name: len(graph.inputs) + i for i, p in enumerate(ordered)
        }
        connections = {(c.processor, c.port): c.source for c in graph.connections}
        sources = np.full((len(ordered), 2), -1, dtype=np.int64)
        kinds: list[int] = []
        state_floors: list[float] = []
        for i, processor in enumerate(ordered):
            ports = sorted(audio_effects.processor_ports(processor))
            if isinstance(processor, audio_effects.Multiply):
                ports = ["carrier", "modulator"]
            for j, port in enumerate(ports):
                source = connections[(processor.name, port)]
                sources[i, j] = (
                    input_indices[source.input]
                    if isinstance(source, audio_effects.InputSource)
                    else processor_indices[source.processor]
                )
            kinds.append(
                0
                if isinstance(processor, audio_effects.Gain)
                else 1
                if isinstance(processor, audio_effects.Multiply)
                else 2
                if isinstance(processor, audio_effects.Filter)
                else 3
            )
            state_floors.append(
                processor.state_floor
                if isinstance(processor, audio_effects.Filter)
                else 0
            )
        frames = end - start
        values = np.zeros((frames, len(ordered), 2))
        filter_values: list[np.ndarray | None] = [None] * len(ordered)
        action_index = 0
        for i in range(frames):
            frame = start + i
            while action_index < len(actions) and actions[action_index].tick == frame:
                self._apply(actions[action_index])
                action_index += 1
            for j, processor in enumerate(ordered):
                state = self.processors[processor.name]
                values[i, j, 1] = state.parameters["mix"].value(
                    frame
                ) * state.bypass.value(frame)
                if isinstance(processor, audio_effects.Gain):
                    values[i, j, 0] = state.parameters["gain_db"].value(frame)
                elif isinstance(processor, audio_effects.SoftClip):
                    values[i, j, 0] = state.parameters["drive"].value(frame)
                elif isinstance(processor, audio_effects.Filter):
                    if (node_filter_values := filter_values[j]) is None:
                        node_filter_values = np.zeros(
                            (frames, len(processor.filters), 2)
                        )
                        filter_values[j] = node_filter_values
                    node_filter_values[i] = [
                        [
                            state.parameters[f"{f.name}-cutoff_hz"].value(frame),
                            state.parameters[f"{f.name}-q"].value(frame),
                        ]
                        for f in processor.filters
                    ]
        native_filters = []
        for i, processor in enumerate(ordered):
            if isinstance(processor, audio_effects.Filter):
                assert filter_values[i] is not None
                native_filters.append(
                    filters.native_inputs(
                        processor.filters,
                        self.processors[processor.name].filter_states,
                        filters.parameters(
                            processor.filters,
                            self.definition.sample_rate,
                            frames,
                            filter_values[i],
                            start,
                        ),
                    )
                )
            else:
                native_filters.append(None)
        output_source = (
            input_indices[graph.output.input]
            if isinstance(graph.output, audio_effects.InputSource)
            else processor_indices[graph.output.processor]
        )
        output, memories = _native.render_effects(
            np.stack([input_audio[v.name] for v in graph.inputs]),
            kinds,
            sources,
            values,
            output_source,
            self.definition.sample_rate,
            native_filters,
            state_floors,
        )
        for i, processor in enumerate(ordered):
            if isinstance(processor, audio_effects.Filter):
                self.processors[processor.name].filter_states = filters.restored_states(
                    memories[i]
                )
        return output

    def _advance_native_granulator(
        self,
        processor: audio_effects.Granulator,
        input_audio: dict[str, np.ndarray],
        actions: list[audio_effects.EffectAction],
        start: int,
        end: int,
    ) -> np.ndarray:
        from . import _native

        state = self.processors[processor.name]
        granular = state.granulator
        assert granular is not None
        frames = end - start
        values = np.zeros((frames, 7))
        action_index = 0
        names = [
            "duration_seconds",
            "density_hz",
            "lookback_seconds",
            "playback_ratio",
            "position_jitter_seconds",
        ]
        for i in range(frames):
            frame = start + i
            while action_index < len(actions) and actions[action_index].tick == frame:
                self._apply(actions[action_index])
                action_index += 1
            values[i, :5] = [state.parameters[n].value(frame) for n in names]
            values[i, 5] = state.parameters["mix"].value(frame) * state.bypass.value(
                frame
            )
            values[i, 6] = granular.frozen
        source = next(iter(input_audio.values()))
        channels = source.shape[1]
        rendered = _native.render_granulator(
            source,
            values,
            start,
            self.definition.sample_rate,
            max(2, round(processor.history_seconds * self.definition.sample_rate)),
            processor.maximum_grains,
            np.asarray(granular.history, dtype=np.float64).reshape(-1, channels),
            granular.history_start,
            granular.phase,
            granular.launch_counter,
            processor.freeze_crossfade_frames,
            [np.asarray(g.samples, dtype=np.float64) for g in granular.grains],
            [g.index for g in granular.grains],
            [g.gain for g in granular.grains],
        )
        (
            output,
            history,
            granular.history_start,
            granular.phase,
            granular.launch_counter,
            grain_samples,
            grain_indices,
            grain_gains,
        ) = rendered
        granular.history = history.tolist()
        if granular.frozen:
            granular.frozen_history = granular.history
            granular.frozen_start = granular.history_start
        granular.grains = [
            GrainState(samples=v.tolist(), index=i, gain=g)
            for v, i, g in zip(grain_samples, grain_indices, grain_gains, strict=True)
        ]
        return output

    def snapshot(self) -> EffectSnapshot:
        return EffectSnapshot(
            definition=self.definition.definition,
            sample_rate=self.definition.sample_rate,
            frame=self.frame,
            processors=self.processors,
            ended_inputs=self.ended_inputs,
            stopped_at=self.stopped_at,
        ).model_copy(deep=True)

    def restore(self, snapshot: EffectSnapshot) -> None:
        if (
            snapshot.definition != self.definition.definition
            or snapshot.sample_rate != self.definition.sample_rate
        ):
            raise EngineError("Snapshot belongs to different prepared effects")
        snapshot = snapshot.model_copy(deep=True)
        self.frame = snapshot.frame
        self.processors = snapshot.processors
        self.ended_inputs = snapshot.ended_inputs
        self.stopped_at = snapshot.stopped_at

    @property
    def drained(self) -> bool:
        return self.stopped_at is not None

    def _apply(self, action: audio_effects.EffectAction) -> None:
        graph = self.definition.definition
        audio_effects.validate_action(graph, action)
        if isinstance(action, audio_effects.InputEndAction):
            if action.input in self.ended_inputs:
                raise ValueError(f"Effect input {action.input} already ended")
            self.ended_inputs[action.input] = action.tick
        elif isinstance(action, audio_effects.StopAction):
            self.stopped_at = action.tick
        elif isinstance(action, audio_effects.ParameterAction):
            state = self.processors[action.processor]
            current = state.parameters[action.parameter]
            state.parameters[action.parameter] = ParameterRamp(
                at=action.tick,
                start=current.value(action.tick),
                target=action.value,
                duration=action.duration_frames,
            )
        elif isinstance(action, audio_effects.BypassAction):
            state = self.processors[action.processor]
            processor = _processor(graph, action.processor)
            state.bypass = ParameterRamp(
                at=action.tick,
                start=state.bypass.value(action.tick),
                target=0.0 if action.bypassed else 1.0,
                duration=processor.bypass_fade_frames,
            )
        elif isinstance(action, audio_effects.FreezeAction):
            state = self.processors[action.processor]
            granular = state.granulator
            if granular is None:
                raise ValueError("Freeze requires the granular processor profile")
            if action.frozen and not granular.frozen:
                granular.frozen_history = [list(v) for v in granular.history]
                granular.frozen_start = granular.history_start
            elif not action.frozen:
                granular.frozen_history = []
            granular.frozen = action.frozen
        else:
            raise ValueError("Unknown effect action")

    def _process_frame(
        self, input_audio: dict[str, np.ndarray], index: int, frame: int
    ) -> tuple[np.ndarray, bool]:
        graph = self.definition.definition
        processors = {p.name: p for p in graph.processors}
        connections = {(c.processor, c.port): c.source for c in graph.connections}
        audio: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}
        ended: dict[str, bool] = {}
        for input in graph.inputs:
            audio[input.name] = (
                np.zeros(len(input.channels))
                if input.name in self.ended_inputs
                else input_audio[input.name][index]
            )
            ended[input.name] = input.name in self.ended_inputs
        processor_audio: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}
        processor_ended: dict[str, bool] = {}
        for name in self.definition.order:
            processor = processors[name]
            ports = {}
            port_ended = {}
            for port in audio_effects.processor_ports(processor):
                source = connections[(name, port)]
                if isinstance(source, audio_effects.InputSource):
                    ports[port] = audio[source.input]
                    port_ended[port] = ended[source.input]
                else:
                    ports[port] = processor_audio[source.processor]
                    port_ended[port] = processor_ended[source.processor]
            processor_audio[name], processor_ended[name] = self._processor_frame(
                processor, ports, port_ended, frame
            )
        if isinstance(graph.output, audio_effects.InputSource):
            return audio[graph.output.input], ended[graph.output.input]
        return (
            processor_audio[graph.output.processor],
            processor_ended[graph.output.processor],
        )

    def _processor_frame(
        self,
        processor: audio_effects.Processor,
        ports: dict[str, np.ndarray],
        ended: dict[str, bool],
        frame: int,
    ) -> tuple[np.ndarray, bool]:
        state = self.processors[processor.name]
        authored_mix = state.parameters["mix"].value(frame)
        mix = authored_mix * state.bypass.value(frame)
        if isinstance(processor, audio_effects.Gain):
            dry = ports["input"]
            wet = dry * pow(10, state.parameters["gain_db"].value(frame) / 20)
            return _mix(dry, wet, mix), ended["input"]
        if isinstance(processor, audio_effects.SoftClip):
            dry = ports["input"]
            drive = state.parameters["drive"].value(frame)
            wet = np.tanh(drive * dry) / np.tanh(drive)
            return _mix(dry, wet, mix), ended["input"]
        if isinstance(processor, audio_effects.Multiply):
            dry = ports["carrier"]
            wet = dry * ports["modulator"]
            return _mix(dry, wet, mix), ended["carrier"]
        if isinstance(processor, audio_effects.Filter):
            dry = ports["input"]
            values = np.array(
                [
                    [
                        state.parameters[f"{f.name}-cutoff_hz"].value(frame),
                        state.parameters[f"{f.name}-q"].value(frame),
                    ]
                    for f in processor.filters
                ]
            )[None, :, :]
            wet, filter_states = filters.filter_samples(
                processor.filters,
                state.filter_states,
                dry[None, :],
                filters.parameters(
                    processor.filters,
                    self.definition.sample_rate,
                    1,
                    values,
                    frame,
                ),
                self.definition.sample_rate,
            )
            state.filter_states = [
                s.model_copy(
                    update={
                        "integrators": [
                            [0 if abs(v) < processor.state_floor else v for v in row]
                            for row in s.integrators
                        ]
                    }
                )
                for s in filter_states
            ]
            drained = ended["input"] and all(
                abs(v) < processor.tail_threshold
                for s in state.filter_states
                for row in s.integrators
                for v in row
            )
            return (
                np.zeros_like(dry) if drained else _mix(dry, wet[0], mix),
                drained,
            )
        if isinstance(processor, audio_effects.Granulator):
            dry = ports["input"]
            wet = self._granulator_frame(processor, state, dry, frame, ended["input"])
            granular = state.granulator
            assert granular is not None
            drained = ended["input"] and not granular.frozen and not granular.grains
            return (np.zeros_like(dry) if drained else _mix(dry, wet, mix), drained)
        if isinstance(processor, audio_effects.TapDelay):
            dry = ports["input"]
            delay = state.tap_delay
            assert delay is not None
            frames = len(delay.history)
            delay_frames = max(
                1,
                round(
                    state.parameters["delay_seconds"].value(frame)
                    * self.definition.sample_rate
                ),
            )
            wet = np.asarray(delay.history[(delay.write - delay_frames) % frames])
            feedback = state.parameters["feedback"].value(frame)
            value = dry if not ended["input"] else np.zeros_like(dry)
            history = value + feedback * wet
            history[np.abs(history) < processor.state_floor] = 0
            delay.history[delay.write] = history.tolist()
            delay.write = (delay.write + 1) % frames
            drained = ended["input"] and all(
                abs(v) < processor.tail_threshold for row in delay.history for v in row
            )
            return (np.zeros_like(dry) if drained else _mix(dry, wet, mix), drained)
        if isinstance(processor, audio_effects.ModulatedDelay):
            dry = ports["input"]
            delay = state.modulated_delay
            assert delay is not None
            frames = len(delay.history)
            phase_offsets = _channel_phase_offsets(processor, len(dry))
            phase = (delay.phase + phase_offsets) % 1
            lfo = _delay_waveform(processor.waveform, phase)
            delays = np.maximum(
                1,
                np.rint(
                    (
                        state.parameters["base_delay_seconds"].value(frame)
                        + state.parameters["depth_seconds"].value(frame) * lfo
                    )
                    * self.definition.sample_rate
                ).astype(np.int64),
            )
            wet = np.asarray(
                [
                    delay.history[(delay.write - value) % frames][channel]
                    for channel, value in enumerate(delays)
                ]
            )
            feedback = state.parameters["feedback"].value(frame)
            value = dry if not ended["input"] else np.zeros_like(dry)
            history = value + feedback * wet
            history[np.abs(history) < processor.state_floor] = 0
            delay.history[delay.write] = history.tolist()
            delay.write = (delay.write + 1) % frames
            delay.phase = (
                delay.phase
                + state.parameters["rate_hz"].value(frame) / self.definition.sample_rate
            ) % 1
            drained = ended["input"] and all(
                abs(v) < processor.tail_threshold for row in delay.history for v in row
            )
            return (np.zeros_like(dry) if drained else _mix(dry, wet, mix), drained)
        raise ValueError("Unknown effect processor")

    def _granulator_frame(
        self,
        processor: audio_effects.Granulator,
        state: ProcessorState,
        dry: np.ndarray,
        frame: int,
        ended: bool,
    ) -> np.ndarray:
        granular = state.granulator
        assert granular is not None
        rate = self.definition.sample_rate
        if not granular.frozen and not ended:
            granular.history.append(dry.tolist())
            maximum = max(2, round(processor.history_seconds * rate))
            if len(granular.history) > maximum:
                granular.history.pop(0)
                granular.history_start += 1
        density = state.parameters["density_hz"].value(frame)
        launch, granular.phase = audio_effects.grain_launches(
            granular.phase, density, rate
        )
        if launch:
            counter = granular.launch_counter
            granular.launch_counter += 1
            if (not ended or granular.frozen) and len(
                granular.grains
            ) < processor.maximum_grains:
                history = (
                    granular.frozen_history if granular.frozen else granular.history
                )
                history_start = (
                    granular.frozen_start if granular.frozen else granular.history_start
                )
                duration = max(
                    2, round(state.parameters["duration_seconds"].value(frame) * rate)
                )
                ratio = state.parameters["playback_ratio"].value(frame)
                lookback = state.parameters["lookback_seconds"].value(frame) * rate
                jitter = (
                    state.parameters["position_jitter_seconds"].value(frame)
                    * rate
                    * audio_effects.grain_jitter(counter)
                )
                end_position = frame - lookback + jitter
                start_position = end_position - (duration - 1) * ratio
                captured = _capture_grain(
                    history,
                    history_start,
                    start_position,
                    ratio,
                    duration,
                    processor.freeze_crossfade_frames if granular.frozen else None,
                )
                if captured is not None:
                    granular.grains.append(
                        GrainState(
                            samples=captured,
                            gain=audio_effects.grain_gain(
                                density,
                                state.parameters["duration_seconds"].value(frame),
                            ),
                        )
                    )
        wet = np.zeros_like(dry)
        active: list[GrainState] = []
        for grain in granular.grains:
            wet += (
                np.asarray(grain.samples[grain.index])
                * audio_effects.grain_window(grain.index, len(grain.samples))
                * grain.gain
            )
            grain.index += 1
            if grain.index < len(grain.samples):
                active.append(grain)
        granular.grains = active
        return wet

def advance(
    self,
    inputs: dict[str, np.ndarray],
    actions: list[audio_effects.EffectAction],
    start: int,
    end: int,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Process `[start, end)`; every input covers that exact frame interval."""
    if start != self.frame or end < start:
        raise EngineError("Effect advance must be contiguous")
    frames = end - start
    graph = self.definition.definition
    if frames > graph.maximum_block_frames:
        raise EngineError("Effect block exceeds its prepared maximum")
    expected = {i.name: len(i.channels) for i in graph.inputs}
    if inputs.keys() != expected.keys():
        raise EngineError("Effect inputs do not match the prepared graph")
    source_audio: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}
    for name, channels in expected.items():
        value = np.asarray(inputs[name], dtype=np.float64)
        if value.shape != (frames, channels) or not np.all(np.isfinite(value)):
            raise EngineError(f"Invalid effect input {name}")
        source_audio[name] = value
    if frames == 0:
        if actions:
            raise EngineError("Zero-frame effect calls cannot contain actions")
        return np.zeros((0, len(self.definition.channels)))
    if any(a.tick < start or a.tick >= end for a in actions):
        raise EngineError("Effect action is outside the render interval")
    if any(
        (b.tick, b.ordinal) <= (a.tick, a.ordinal)
        for a, b in zip(actions, actions[1:], strict=False)
    ):
        raise EngineError("Effect actions must be strictly ordered")
    action_index = 0
    output = np.zeros((frames, len(self.definition.channels)))
    try:
        if (
            self.backend == "native"
            and not any(
                isinstance(
                    a, (audio_effects.InputEndAction, audio_effects.StopAction)
                )
                for a in actions
            )
            and not self.ended_inputs
            and _native_supported(self.processors, graph, actions)
        ):
            output = self._advance_native(source_audio, actions, start, end)
            self.frame = end
            return output
        for i in range(frames):
            frame = start + i
            while (
                action_index < len(actions) and actions[action_index].tick == frame
            ):
                self._apply(actions[action_index])
                action_index += 1
            if self.stopped_at is not None:
                continue
            audio, ended = self._process_frame(source_audio, i, frame)
            if ended:
                self.stopped_at = frame
            else:
                output[i] = audio
    except (ValueError, FloatingPointError) as error:
        self.stopped_at = start
        output.fill(0)
        raise EngineError(
            f"Effect processing failed in block at frame {start}"
        ) from error
    if not np.all(np.isfinite(output)):
        self.stopped_at = start
        output.fill(0)
        raise EngineError(f"Non-finite effect output in block at frame {start}")
    self.frame = end
    return output

class OfflineEffectAttachment:
    """Apply a one-input graph to any offline engine with `advance`."""

    def __init__(self, source: object, effects: OfflineEffects) -> None:
        graph = effects.definition.definition
        main = [
            i for i in graph.inputs if isinstance(i.source, audio_effects.MainStream)
        ]
        if len(graph.inputs) != 1 or len(main) != 1:
            raise EngineError("Offline attachment requires a main-only effect graph")
        self.source = source
        self.effects = effects
        self.input = main[0].name

    def advance(
        self,
        source_actions: list[object],
        effect_actions: list[audio_effects.EffectAction],
        start: int,
        end: int,
    ) -> np.ndarray:
        advance = getattr(self.source, "advance", None)
        if not isinstance(advance, Callable):
            raise EngineError("Attached source has no advance method")
        return self.effects.advance(
            {self.input: advance(source_actions, start, end)},
            effect_actions,
            start,
            end,
        )

def process_audio(
    definition: PreparedEffects,
    inputs: dict[str, np.ndarray],
    actions: list[audio_effects.EffectAction] | None = None,
    backend: Literal["numpy", "native"] = "numpy",
    block_frames: int | None = None,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Process complete named streams through one prepared graph in blocks."""
    frames = {v.shape[0] for v in inputs.values()}
    if len(frames) != 1:
        raise EngineError("Effect input streams must have equal lengths")
    total = frames.pop()
    block_frames = block_frames or definition.definition.maximum_block_frames
    if block_frames <= 0 or block_frames > definition.definition.maximum_block_frames:
        raise EngineError("Effect block size exceeds its prepared maximum")
    renderer = OfflineEffects(definition, backend)
    actions = actions or []
    output = np.zeros((total, len(definition.channels)))
    cursor = 0
    for start in range(0, total, block_frames):
        end = min(total, start + block_frames)
        first = cursor
        while cursor < len(actions) and actions[cursor].tick < end:
            cursor += 1
        output[start:end] = renderer.advance(
            {n: v[start:end] for n, v in inputs.items()},
            actions[first:cursor],
            start,
            end,
        )
    return output
